name: Arcturus Defense Solutions Ballistic Chaff Dispenser BCD-3 'Static Veil'
product_name: Arcturus Defense Solutions Ballistic Chaff Dispenser BCD-3 'Static Veil'
description:
The BCD-3 is a burst-deployment personal countermeasure system that ejects a dense cloud of 40,000 magnetically-charged ferrofluid micro-pellets in a 270-degree arc around the wearer within 12 milliseconds of activation. Each pellet is 0.8mm, tungsten-carbide coated, and carries a magnetic charge sufficient to perturb the trajectory of any ferromagnetic projectile — coilgun rounds, magnetically-stabilized smart ammunition, and any round with significant ferrous content — by 3-7 degrees at ranges up to 4 meters. Against conventional brass-jacketed rounds, the physical density of 40,000 pellets in a 1.5-meter cloud creates a probabilistic interference layer: not reliable deflection, but meaningful trajectory degradation against the first volley.

The Static Veil was designed specifically as a counter to coilgun weapons, which now represent the most prevalent military-grade threat in GLMZ. A coilgun round's ferromagnetic penetrator, the Arcturus engineering team noted, is inherently susceptible to the same magnetic manipulation that makes it fast in the first place. The BCD-3 essentially turns the weapon's own technology against it. Against standard 9mm and 5.56mm the cloud provides roughly 40% first-volley degradation — enough, in a firefight, to matter.

The BCD-3 is single-use. After deployment, the dispenser cartridge is spent. Reload takes 8 seconds under ideal conditions, 25 under fire. Operators typically carry 3-6 reload cartridges. The pellet cloud disperses in approximately 4 seconds and is not harmful to the wearer or nearby allies beyond a stinging sensation at close range. The activation trigger is a thumb-press on the wrist mount — fast enough that trained operators can activate in the moment they hear the first shot, relying on the 12ms deployment speed to cover the gap between human reaction time and ballistic arrival.
legality: Restricted — licensed security and above; Prohibited — civilian
tactical_use: Best used as a one-shot reaction to ambush — activate the instant you hear fire, use the 4-second cloud window to relocate behind cover. Not a sustained defense. Against a single shooter with a coilgun, the BCD-3 buys almost guaranteed survival of the first volley and time to break contact. Against multiple shooters or automatic fire, the cloud is quickly overwhelmed by volume. Primary tactical use: bodyguard bump — when a principal is hit in the open, the escort activates BCD-3 to cover the 4-second drag to cover. In corponation security doctrine, at least one member of any 3-person detail carries a BCD-3 for exactly this purpose.
cultural_context: The BCD-3 is Tier 3 accessible — expensive but not stratospheric. A successful B-tier freelancer with a profitable run can afford one. This has made the Static Veil the most common serious personal protection item on the GLMZ security market below the IVS-7 swarm systems. Arcturus sells roughly 80,000 BCD-3 cartridges per month in GLMZ alone. The device has also created a counter-market: coilgun round manufacturers have begun producing non-ferrous 'chaff-proof' penetrators specifically to defeat BCD-3 systems, and Arcturus is now on BCD-4 development. The old military-industrial arms race, miniaturized to personal scale.
story_hooks: Someone has been modifying BCD-3 cartridges to deploy a neurotoxin mixed into the pellet cloud — the Arcturus countermeasure is now a murder weapon, and nobody knows how many units are compromised.
The new BCD-3R 'Reaper' cartridge — rumored, not officially confirmed — allegedly deploys razor-edged pellets instead of rounded ones. A chaff cloud that strips skin. Someone has one.
